57: Discussion. Ash is the residue remaining after ignition and represents the total inorganic contribution of the grain. Ash follows the germ and aleurone, which carry the greater part of the mineral matter, so that cultivars with a thicker aleurone or a larger embryo return higher values.
58: Comparable results have been published elsewhere. Hu et al. (2019) determined that ash follows the proportion of germ and aleurone surviving; Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) that the spread in ash derives from the outer grain layers; Jannasch and Wang (2020) that the steeping medium may augment the mineral fraction; and Kumar et al. (2022) that ash is redistributed rather than lost on treatment. Dudeshwar returned the most favourable value in every product of this group and is therefore the cultivar to select where a high value is required.

65: Discussion. Phenolic acids are the principal antioxidants of the grain and are largely bound to the pericarp cell wall, so that a higher retained content in the product is preferable. The greater part of the phenolic acid is bound to arabinoxylan in the pericarp wall; heat cleaves these bonds and liberates it while concurrently degrading and leaching the free fraction, so that the value recorded represents the balance of the two processes.

(2025) that soaking and cooking reduce phenolic acids, the bound fraction exceeding the free. The leading cultivar varied with the product, Kalonunia, Kataribhog and Lal Badshabhog ranking highest in turn, so that no single recommendation covers the group on this attribute.

72: Discussion. Flavonoids contribute to antioxidant activity and to pericarp colour. They degrade readily on heating, so that the residual content indicates the gentleness of the treatment applied. Flavonoids are synthesised in the pericarp and cultivars differ in the quantity deposited; being readily destroyed by heat, their residual content reflects both the initial level and the treatment.

79: Discussion. Antioxidant capacity measures the activity of the entire bioactive fraction rather than its quantity, so that a higher value is desirable. It derives from the surviving phenolics and flavonoids together with the browning products formed during heating, so that cultivars rich in bound phenolics retain more of it.

(2023) that browning products contribute to the measured activity. 86: Discussion. Phytic acid chelates iron, zinc and calcium in the intestine and precludes their absorption, so that a lower content is preferable, since it liberates the very minerals the grain supplies. Phytate is deposited as globoids in the aleurone during grain filling and is hydrolysed by endogenous phytase during soaking, so that the residue is contingent upon both processes.
87: This is consistent with previous studies. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that treated brown rice retains approximately half the phytate of untreated grain; Kumar et al. (2022) that reduced phytate corresponds to greater iron and zinc absorption; Bhar et al. (2022) that the reduction of phytate constitutes a principal nutritional argument for processed grain; and Hu et al. (2019) that germination and hydrothermal treatment operate by different mechanisms. No single cultivar proved superior across all the products: Dudeshwar, Gobindabhog and Kalonunia ranked highest in different ones, so that the decision is contingent upon the product concerned.

94: Discussion. Copper is required for iron transport and for several enzymes, cereals constituting a principal dietary source, so that a higher content in the product is preferable. Copper is translocated into the grain by COPT and HMA transporters and sequestered principally in the aleurone, so that cultivars of greater uptake and translocation capacity accumulate more.

101: Discussion. Iron deficiency is the commonest nutritional disorder among rice-eating populations, so that the iron retained in the product is of direct importance and a higher content is preferable. Grain iron is contingent upon the quantity remobilised from the flag leaf and upon the chelators effecting its transport, both of which differ between cultivars, while cooking translocates a proportion of it inward from the pericarp.
102: The same pattern has been reported previously. Sonu et al. (2025) determined that grain iron is heritable but that few lines attain nutritional targets; Kumar et al. (2022) that iron migrates inward and becomes more available; Jannasch and Wang (2020) that the steep water may convey iron and calcium into the endosperm; and Akter et al. (2025) that iron declined while protein and zinc were concentrated. The leading cultivar varied with the product, Kalojira and Kalonunia ranking highest in turn, so that no single recommendation covers the group on this attribute.
